newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY - Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe wrote a declaration criticising the Communist Party of betraying its own history. He had escaped to Hong Kong and was on his way to the United States.

-- MING PAO - A four-hour gala party would be held on the evening of June 30 through the morning of July 1, to celebrate the Hong Kong 1997 handover. China will spend 10 million yuan to organise a 600-strong group to take part in the performances.
-- TA KUNG PAO - A new book, Why China Says No, was published in Beijing, saying there was no anti-American sentiment on the mainland and accusing the U.S. of starting a new cold war against China.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY - Hong Kong Police have received calls threatening to get revenge for Hong Kong's Diaoyu (Senkaku) Islands protests by placing bombs in the subway.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - New World Development plans to boost its investment in property development in Guangzhou. It said it was confident about the property market and the new leadership of the city.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - China's already struggling vehicle industry has suffered a new blow in a decision to abandon a short-lived experiment with car loans.
-- China issued another strong signal yesterday that its stock and bond markets had been approved for fast growth to provide the economy with more efficient means of investment.
-- HONG KONG STANDARD -- Some shark's fin in Hong Kong contained more than 10 times the "safe" mercury level and might pose a significant health danger.
-- Shanghai-based brokers said Beijing's eighth bonds issue of the year was another sign Beijing would soon cut rates again.
